newsitem.title: USA: NYC MAC staff asks board to okay deal with city.
newsitem.headline: NYC MAC staff asks board to okay deal with city.

text.p: The head of the Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC) for the City of New York on Wednesday said he will ask the board to approve a plan for the city to sell bonds and exchange the cash for debt owned by the MAC.

The manoeuvre will enable the city to avoid hitting a constitutional limit on how much debt it can issue until late in the 1997 fiscal year, which ends on June 30. Earlier this week, city officials said they expected to hit the debt cap in a couple of months.
New York City plans to sell $625 million of new money bonds during the week of December 16 and exchange the cash for around $600 million of city bonds that the MAC holds.
The MAC, which was set up to rescue the city from its mid-1980 financial crisis, said that from its credit and market perspective the transaction was a non-event.
"We would simply replace the lost debt service revenues with a larger draw on sales tax," said Quentin Spector, the executive director of MAC, in prepared remarks.

"Since preserving the city's access to the capital markets is a key MAC mission, and since honoring this request has no consequence for MAC, it was an easy decision to direct staff to cooperate with the City to resolve the technical barriers to the transaction, which they have accomplished."
Spector said he will recommend that the Board authorize the arrangement at a previously scheduled meeting on December 12.
